trajectory: Fix rounds in order. r9 found that the page resolution effect re-resolved after an impossible stretch. The r10 fix (3fd99e10e) took the `impossible` gate off the launcher data hooks, which removed a state. In the page effect it kept the `impossible` branch, changing it from clear to return, and added a held-resolution reuse branch backed by two new refs (inResolutionRef, resolvedRetryToken), which added state. This round (26001fc02) adds one more `!impossible` guard, on the derived `inNameState` (useFolderFiles.ts:354-360). It removes nothing. The guard repeats a prediction that earlier rounds already placed on `inNameBlocked` (:353) and `inNamePending` (:801), and on the effect itself (:302). So each round has added another `impossible` check in the same in: resolution area to undo a side effect of the previous one: the design is being patched, not restructured. The page now handles `impossible` in four separate places, while the window handles it in a single early branch. This round's change is small and correct for what it targets.
specification_compliance: r10 D3/R1 is fixed. useFolderFiles.ts:354-360 now reports inNameState as null while `impossible`, so FolderContent.tsx:141 and PassageList.tsx:349 no longer render a held refused, failed or tooLarge notice, and FolderBrowser.tsx:874 can show the empty state. This matches spec sending step 1 precedence (impossible first) and the window's behaviour (useFileSearch clears inNameError on its impossible branch).

The held resolution itself is untouched (activeResolution :350-351 is still keyed only by inKey), so the I28/I29 fix from r10 survives: when the query becomes possible again with the same in: key, the held status or members come back without resolving again.
The dead 再試行 noted in r10's unspecified list no longer appears: with inNameState null while impossible, no retry control is rendered.
I7/I18 still hold. The effect returns at :302 and fetchPage returns empty for conditionsImpossible, so nothing is requested.

The new test in SearchPage.negation.test.tsx ('an impossible query shows the empty state, not a held refused notice') would fail if the `!impossible &&` guard were removed, because the refused text would stay. It kills that mutation.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: During an impossible stretch with a held resolved in: resolution, trackFirstPage marks that resolution as listed after the (request-free) empty page, so when the query becomes possible again inNamePending is already false before the real first page arrives.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: After editing an in: query through a contradiction and back, the page may for one render show the reset listing's empty state or a 0 count before loading starts, instead of the pending state the in: gate normally gives.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A -in: name that matches no collection of the drive (a typo) is sent as exclude_collection and silently excludes nothing.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Typing '-in:Tirp' shows an Exclude chip over unfiltered results with no hint that the name matched nothing.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A held failed, tooLarge or refused notice for an in: key reappears, without resolving again, when an intervening impossible edit is undone.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Removing the contradicting token brings back the same notice as before; only 再試行 or a key change resolves again, as I28 asks.

regression_risks: The page now gates `impossible` separately in the effect, inNameBlocked, inNameState and inNamePending. A future derived value read from activeResolution, such as resolvedFileIds or resolvedCollections, could show held state during an impossible stretch unless it is guarded too.
The held-resolution reuse depends on render-mirrored refs (inResolutionRef, resolvedRetryToken). Changes to how inResolution is set could make a needed resolution get skipped.
test_coverage: The new SearchPage test covers a held 'refused' status followed by an impossible edit. No test covers a held 'failed' status (with its 再試行) or 'tooLarge' in the same sequence, but they go through the same guard.
No test covers the passages view (PassageList) showing the impossible state over a held notice.
No test covers undoing the impossible edit after a held refused status and asserting that the notice comes back without new list requests.
